meta.title: 120th House Freshman Tracker
meta.maintainer: Soren Dayton, Foundation for American Innovation
meta.disclaimer: Evolving work product built from open-source research; not validated against primary records. Caucus memberships are predictions.

changelog.t: Races called: Eli Crane (R) held AZ-2 over Jonathan Nez, 162,741–158,857 (AP, 11/09), and Mario Díaz-Balart (R) held FL-26 over Nicole Locklin, 114,578–112,874 (AP, 11/09); both challengers removed. CO-4 marked Called for Eileen Laubacher on CNN's projection, AP pending. FL-27 machine recount under way; MN-1 margin now 321 ahead of 11/19 certification.

Added a Confirmed level (C) above the predicted levels H, M and L. C means the caucus or the member has publicly named someone as a member or incoming member; each confirmed tag keeps the level it was predicted at. First confirmations: CAPAC for Dandiya, Koh, Pan and Shah. Added Guam's delegate-elect Alicia Limtiaco (D), who unseated James Moylan; the original sweep covered delegate seats that opened but not one that changed hands.

Weekly caucus update. Blue Dog: the Blue Dog PAC's list of backed winners raised Mendoza (AZ-6) and Dembo (KY-6) to new High tags and Ager, Cooke and Forstag to High. Progressive Caucus: CPC PAC endorsements raised nine members to High (Forstag, Padilla Stout, Brooks, García, McGuire, White, Little, Lasher, Poindexter). Poindexter's Blue Dog tag stays Low because sources conflict. CAPAC's 11/04 release is noted on four rows. Caucus-level announcements added to the method section.

Added two Democratic challengers the original sweep missed because their uncalled races had incumbent leaders: Tessa Lynn Hodge (CA-23, trails Obernolte by 2.8 pts) and Nicole Locklin (FL-26, trails Díaz-Balart by 0.7 pts). Both fall inside the page's 3-point rule for trailers. A full check of every uncalled race found no other omissions.

RG2 corrected against its public member list (47 members, on the group's PAC site), which the earlier method section wrongly said did not exist. Yesterday's audit over-corrected: about a third of listed members hold R+10 or redder seats and half hold R+7 or redder, many of them appropriators, so a competitive seat is one route into RG2, not the only one. Tags now go to freshmen with a specific route (a competitive seat, succeeding a listed member, or an Appropriations or Agriculture background) and no record pointing the other way: Elijah, Kingston, McKinney, Gaines, Sell and Hatcher. Steinmann, Gober and Alfonso stay untagged.

Republican Governance Group guesses cut from 14 to 1 after an audit. The original tags leaned on Main Street PAC endorsements, which in 2026 also went to movement-right candidates in safe seats (an AFPI general counsel, America PAC's chief counsel, a Bongino Show producer). RG2 members mostly come from seats where a moderate brand pays; only FL-7 (R+5) clears that bar.

Races called: Mark Lamb (AZ-5, R), Anthony Constantino (NY-21, R), Victoria Broderick (TN-4, D). Dan Green (FL-9) and Colby Watson (NC-8) removed after their races were called against them. Margins refreshed for all twelve uncalled rows from state election boards and local reporting, and each uncalled or runoff row now links to the official state results page: recounts pending or requested in MN-1, FL-27 and SC-2; NC-3, NC-5 and NC-7 inside recount range ahead of the 11/13 canvass; FL-7 a hair outside; CA-4, CO-4, AZ-2 and WA-5 still counting. Added Open Graph, Search Console, Dataset metadata, per-member links, and data.csv. Every row now links to its Ballotpedia race page. Member links are now taken from each race's own candidate listing instead of being built from the name; that fixed 51 of 242 links that were broken: 22 on Ballotpedia (13 disambiguation pages, 9 missing) and 29 on Wikipedia (10 pointed at a different person of the same name, 15 at disambiguation pages, 4 at nothing useful). Six members have no Wikipedia article, so that link is omitted for them.

Added Republican Governance Group as a guess-only (Low) tag on 14 Republicans, with FEC context on the group's 2026 giving. Added leadership-role flags (chamber leadership, committee chair, vice chair/subcommittee) for prior legislative service. Converted method section to bullets. Published to GitHub Pages with data.js and data.json.

Initial release: every open or flipped House seat and the two open delegate seats, with called winners, leaders and trailers in uncalled races, and the Louisiana runoffs; prior legislative service, committee assignments, and predicted ideological and identity caucus memberships.
